simple.meaning: חָדָשׁ (châdâsh) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “new.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 53 times across Exodus, Leviticus, Numbers, Deuteronomy, Joshua, and 15 more, beginning at Exodus 1:8. Its contexts include offering, blood, kingship, Egypt.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to חָדָשׁ (H2319).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: חָדָשׁ (châdâsh) / H2319 is traced through Exodus 1:8, Leviticus 23:16, Leviticus 26:10, Numbers 28:26 as a generated source-based concept entry.
